description: Search the web, news, images, scholarly papers, companies and people in one call. 2 credits per 10 results from each ...

categories.description: pdf: web results that are PDF files. research: scholarly papers, in a research list, ranked by relevance then citations. companies: companies that match the query, in a companies list, best matches first. The query can name a place, industry, employee count, founding year and funding stage, like fintech startups in Berlin, 50-200 employees. people: people that match the query, in a people list, best matches first. The query can name a role, company, place or research topic, like CFO of Stripe, founders of fintech startups in Berlin, or researchers on CRISPR base editing. Each person has roles, affiliations and public profile links, never contact details. developer: passages from GitHub READMEs, issues, merged pull requests, releases, developer docs and API operations, in a developer list; send it as an object to filter by repos, types, language and minStars. videos: passages from what is said in YouTube videos shared under a Creative Commons license, in a videos list, one result per video, with the channel, the license and the watch link; the link carries &t= only when the passage's start is exact. The index is a June 2024 snapshot of English videos, so a link may be dead.

language.description: Only repositories whose main language is this, like TypeScript.

minStars.description: Only repositories with at least this many GitHub stars.

repos.description: Only results from these GitHub repositories, as owner/name.

types.description: Only these result types: readme, issue, pull_request, release, operation, doc.

country.description: Two-letter country to search from, like us. Image results are always US.

domainTools.description: Accepted for compatibility. We have no domain-matched tools to add, so true and false give the same results.

highlights.description: On by default. When a web result's page is already stored, its description is the passages of that page that best match the query. Send false for the snippet the search engine shows.

ignoreInvalidURLs.description: Leave out results whose address cannot be read as a page.

limit.description: Most results to return for each source. Default 10, or 5 with scrapeOptions, which reads every web result returned. News returns at most 50.

location.description: Where to search from, like Germany or San Francisco,California,United States. The last part is the country and replaces country. A city before it narrows web results to that place.

maxAge.description: Accept a stored answer up to this many milliseconds old, at most 30 days. Without it, 15 minutes for news and 1 hour for web and images. 0 always searches live.

safe.description: Hide explicit web and image results when true.

scrapeOptions.description: Reads each web result, as many as limit asks for, within timeout, and puts the passages that best match the query in each description. Takes the options of scrape: formats (markdown, html, rawHtml, links, images, summary, screenshot, json and the rest), onlyMainContent, includeTags, excludeTags, maxAge, minAge, waitFor, mobile, timeout (per page), headers, actions, location, parsers, profile and zeroDataRetention. Costs what scrape costs for each page read: 1 credit, plus 4 for each summary or json with a schema or prompt that returns something.

actions.description: Up to 50 steps to run on the page, in order, before reading it: { "type": "wait", "milliseconds": 500 } (up to 30 seconds), { "type": "wait", "selector": ".results" }, { "type": "click", "selector": "button.more" }, { "type": "write", "text": "tides" }, { "type": "press", "key": "Enter" }, { "type": "scroll", "direction": "down" } (also up, left or right; amount is pixels, "viewport" or "max"; maxScrolls 1 to 50; selector scrolls an inner container; "max" keeps scrolling until the page stops growing, for feeds that load as you go), { "type": "screenshot", "fullPage": true } (links come back in actions.screenshots), { "type": "scrape" } (the page at that point, in actions.scrapes), { "type": "executeJavascript", "script": "document.title" } (results in actions.javascriptReturns), { "type": "pdf", "format": "A4" } (links in actions.pdfs) or { "type": "perform", "action": "Click the Load more button" } (a step in plain words, up to 5 browser steps on this page, never leaving the site; at most 5 per call). A read with actions costs 1 credit, the same as any page; the actions themselves add nothing. If an action fails, you still get the page as it stood, with a warning that names the action and says why.

blockAds.description: Ads and trackers are not loaded when a page runs in a browser. Send false to load them.

checkPromptInjection.description: Send true to scan the page text for instructions aimed at an AI model before anything is built from it. A page that has them is refused with 403 promptInjectionDetected and costs nothing. The scan adds 4 credits when it runs; a page it cannot scan fully comes back with a warning and no charge.

excludeTags.description: Remove the parts of the page that match these CSS selectors, such as .comments.

fastMode.description: Send true to read the page without opening a browser: the answer comes sooner, but a page that needs a browser, or that refuses a plain request, comes back as an error instead of being retried. Ignored when the call needs a browser (actions, screenshot, waitFor, mobile, profile, network, branding).

formats.description: What to return: markdown (clean page text), summary (a short summary of the page), html (the cleaned page), rawHtml (the page as sent), audio and video (for a YouTube link: the audio track as an M4A file, or the video as an MP4 file, as a link that works for 1 hour), rawBase64 (the bytes the site sent, Base64 encoded, from a live read; metadata.contentType says what they are), links (every link on the page), images (every image address), screenshot (a link to a JPEG of the visible page, kept for 7 days), changeTracking (what changed in the markdown since your key last read this page with the same options, kept 30 days; add modes ["git-diff","json"] with a schema or prompt to compare fields too), question (send { "type": "question", "question": "..." } to get answer, null when the page does not state one), product (title, brand, category, url, description and variants with price, sale, availability and images, or null) and menu (merchant, currency and sections of items with prices, or null) network (the JSON the page loaded while it rendered, up to 30 responses) and branding (the page's colors, fonts, typography, spacing, button and input styles, logo and brand images, read from how the page looks, with a field left out when the page does not show it). Send { "type": "screenshot", "fullPage": true } for the whole page. Send { "type": "highlights", "query": "refund policy" } for the passages that best match a query. Send { "type": "json", "schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "price": { "type": "number" } } } } or { "type": "json", "prompt": "the price and the stock" } for fields filled from the page, each checked against it. Send { "type": "json", "parser": "amazon-product" } to get a site's own data as json instead of reading the page; GET /v1/parsers lists the parsers. Send { "type": "json", "rules": { "title": "h1", "links": { "selector": "a", "type": "list", "output": "@href" } } } to read the page with CSS rules and no model, at the page's own price. Send { "type": "attributes", "selectors": [{ "selector": "a", "attribute": "href" }] } for attribute values, returned in attributes. Without a parser or rules, json needs a schema or a prompt and is filled from the page. json with a schema or a prompt, summary, highlights, question, product, menu and changeTracking in json mode cost 4 credits more each when they return something. json with rules or a parser, and attributes, cost nothing more. A screenshot, network or branding read costs 1 credit, the same as any page. A PDF comes back as markdown only, and costs 1 credit more for each page read.

modes.description: git-diff returns a unified diff of the markdown. json compares the fields in schema or prompt between this read and the last one. Without modes you get git-diff.

prompt.description: With json mode: what to compare, in plain words, such as the price and stock.

schema.description: The fields to fill, as a JSON Schema (draft-07 or 2020-12) object with properties. Pydantic's model_json_schema() and zod's toJSONSchema() output work as they are. enum, const, anyOf, oneOf, nullable types, $ref with $defs, required, descriptions and any key names are read. Up to 100 top-level fields and 32 KB. A field the page does not state comes back null.

question.description: A question to answer from the page, such as what the refund window is.

fullPage.description: Capture the whole page from top to bottom instead of the visible part.

quality.description: JPEG quality from 1 to 100. The default is 70.

viewport.description: The window size in pixels, such as { width: 390, height: 844 }.

count.description: How many passages to return, best match first.

query.description: What you are looking for on the page, such as refund policy.

checkPromptInjection.description: Deprecated: send checkPromptInjection at the top level of the call.

options.description: Only with parser: extra inputs for it, such as { "page": 2 } for the next page of results or { "minRating": 4.5 } for a filter. GET /v1/parsers lists what each parser accepts.

parser.description: Read the page with a named parser, which gives the site's own data as json. The url must be the kind of page the parser reads. Parsers are the only way to read some sites. GET /v1/parsers lists them.

prompt.description: What to pull from the page in plain words, such as the version and the release date.

rules.description: Read the page with CSS rules instead of a model, no extra fee. Each field is a selector such as "h1" (the first match's text), "a@href" (an attribute) or { "selector": "li", "type": "list", "output": "text" | "html" | "@attribute" | { nested fields } }. A missing item is null and an unmatched list is []. Relative links become absolute. Up to 100 fields, 5 levels deep. Not with schema, prompt or parser.

schema.description: The fields to fill, as a JSON Schema (draft-07 or 2020-12) object with properties. Pydantic's model_json_schema() and zod's toJSONSchema() output work as they are. enum, const, anyOf, oneOf, nullable types, $ref with $defs, required, descriptions and any key names are read. Up to 100 top-level fields and 32 KB. A field the page does not state comes back null.

selectors.description: The elements and attributes to read, such as { selector: 'a.buy', attribute: 'href' }.

headers.description: Extra request headers to send to the site, such as { "x-plan": "pro" }. A read with headers is never answered from or saved to a stored copy.

includeTags.description: Keep only the parts of the page that match these CSS selectors, such as article or .price. When set, onlyMainContent is not applied.

location.description: Where to read the page from. The default is the United States.

country.description: Two-letter country code to read the page from, such as DE or JP.

languages.description: Languages to ask the site for, best first, such as ["de", "en"]. Sent as Accept-Language. A read with languages is never answered from or saved to a stored copy.

lockdown.description: Send true to answer only from a stored copy of the page and never read it live, whatever its age. A page with no stored copy is notFound. The same as minAge 0.

maxAge.description: Accept a stored answer up to this many milliseconds old, at most 30 days. Without it, 2 days, or less for a site whose pages change often, and a copy up to twice that age (at most 7 days) comes back at once as stale while a fresh read runs. 0 always reads the page live. metadata.cacheState says which one you got.

minAge.description: Answer only from a stored copy that is at least this many milliseconds old, and never read the page live. 0 accepts any stored copy. A page with no such copy is notFound.

mobile.description: Read the page as a phone would: a phone-sized screen and the mobile version of the site. The page loads in a browser.

onlyCleanContent.description: Send true to have a model remove what onlyMainContent leaves behind in the markdown: cookie banners, ads, share widgets, breadcrumbs, sign-up prompts, comment prompts and related-article lists. It only removes whole paragraphs and lists; it never rewrites or adds text, and code blocks are always kept. Skipped with a warning when the page is too long to clean or the model does not answer. Not with zeroDataRetention. Summary, answers and highlights are made from the cleaned markdown.

onlyMainContent.description: Keep only the page's main content, without menus, headers, footers and ads.

parsers.description: Only the pdf parser exists. Send "pdf" or { "type": "pdf", mode, maxPages, pages, blocks, pageMarkers } with the same meaning as in parse. Without mode a PDF is read from its text layer only; auto reads the picture of a page that has no text, and ocr reads the picture of every page, up to 20 pages. Each page read costs 1 credit.

blocks.description: Send true to also get the page's layout in blocks: each title, section header or run of text, with its page, reading order, position on the page (bbox as left, top, right, bottom from 0 to 1) and where its text sits in that page's markdown (span, as in pages). Tables, figures and formulas are not told apart. A page read from its picture is one block. No extra charge.

maxPages.description: Read at most this many pages, up to 100.

mode.description: fast reads the text layer only. auto (the default) reads the text layer and reads the picture of any page that has none. ocr reads the picture of every page.

pageMarkers.description: Send true to mark page breaks in the markdown: pages are joined with "---" and a <!-- page N --> line, where N is the page that follows. No extra charge.

pages.description: Send true to also get each page's markdown in pages, as { pageNumber, markdown }. No extra charge.

profile.description: Read the page with the cookies and local storage that earlier calls saved under this name, kept for your account for 30 days after the last use. A call with a profile always loads the page in a browser, costs 1 credit, the same as any page, and is never answered from a stored copy. Only one call at a time can save to a profile.

name.description: A name you choose, such as shop-login. Calls with the same name share state.

saveChanges.description: Keep the cookies and local storage this read leaves behind for the next call with this name. Send false to read with the profile without changing it.

proxy.description: Which route reads the page. auto and basic start with the cheapest route and move up when the site refuses. enhanced starts on a residential browser. The price is the same.

entities.description: What to hide: PERSON, EMAIL, PHONE, LOCATION, FINANCIAL, SECRET. All by default.

mode.description: accurate finds names and places with the model and the rest by pattern. aggressive adds guesses that catch more and may hide a little too much. fast uses patterns only, so it finds no ordinary names or places.

replaceStyle.description: tag writes <EMAIL>, mask writes * for each character, remove deletes it.

redactPII.description: Send true, or an object, to hide personal data in the markdown and in everything made from it (summary, answers, highlights, json). Links, html and rawHtml are not changed. A page the model cannot scan is refused rather than returned unredacted.

removeBase64Images.description: Images inside the page that carry their data in the address (data:image) are dropped by default. Send false to keep them in markdown and html.

skipTlsVerification.description: Send true to read a page whose certificate is expired, self-signed or for another name. The read is not private against someone between us and the site.

storeInCache.description: Send false to neither read nor keep a stored copy of this page.

timeout.description: How long to keep trying, in milliseconds, between 10 seconds and 2 minutes. Pages behind a bot check can need 10 to 30 seconds the first time.

waitFor.description: Extra milliseconds to wait before reading, up to 60000, for pages that load their content late. To wait for an element, add a wait action with a selector. A read that waits costs 1 credit, the same as any page.

zeroDataRetention.description: Send true to keep nothing from this call: no stored copy is read or made, and nothing from it is logged. Costs 1 credit more per page. Not with a screenshot.

sources.description: What to search: web, news, images. Each is a string or {type}. The catalogue names alexandria and exchange are accepted and left out: they name a source we do not have. Default web, or none when categories asks for research, companies, people, developer or videos.

tbs.description: Time filter: qdr:h, qdr:d, qdr:w, qdr:m or qdr:y, or cdr:1,cd_min:MM/DD/YYYY,cd_max:MM/DD/YYYY. Web takes both; news takes qdr only; images take none.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the sources.

title: Search
